summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 17th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with no significant side effects. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, falling below 0.1 by discharge, with no renal toxicity. Liver enzymes showed mild, expected elevation. A recent brain MRI confirmed stable disease without new lesions. Due to her history of DVT and PE, aspirin was held during admission to optimize methotrexate excretion and was restarted at discharge. She remained emotionally stable on citalopram, with no depressive symptoms. Chronic right foot pain was managed with gabapentin and PRN oxycodone. She was discharged home in good condition with instructions to restart aspirin and follow up for her next chemotherapy cycle.
